what: About 420 star dots fill the sky in every frame; next to the 3,000 data dots they read as stray data marks, and stars are decoration on an ink-and-clean manager stage.
why: In a film where every dot is one moment of one orbit, no dot may be scenery: zero stars makes every mark on screen a datum (I2 visible) and keeps the exec stage ink and clean.

what: The cut plane is seen at about 13 degrees, so the lit specks on it squash into one flat band; 'each cut shows rings' is told by caption, the six rings are not visible.
why: Ending the cut at 38 degrees opens the plane into a disc so the concentric rings of lit specks separate; with M1 landing at 30 degrees (next finding) the cut tilts only 8 degrees in 5 s, inside R-E P6 (slice x hold or slow orbit). Round 2: check the 62 pin clears the plane edge.

what: M1 lands at 20 degrees; the cut that follows needs a higher view, and starting it from 20 would make the slice a 18-degree tilt.
why: Nested spheres project the same from any elevation, so landing M1 at 30 degrees costs the shell view nothing and lets the cut stay almost still (T5, one change at a time). Round 2: check M2 still lands flat on the five layers.

what: At the landing the 300 specks on 6 shells project into one filled disc; the dotted guide rings that mark the shells are almost invisible (wireDim 0.45).
why: Brighter guides outline the six shells and, in the cut, the six rings, so 'thin shells' has a picture; the HOOK floor rings get brighter too (check round 2).

what: The cut's counts live only in a 14-unit pin ('62 ORBITS LIT, 620 OF 3,000 DOTS'); the caption 'The cut keeps the orbits near the equator lit' carries no count and uses 'equator'.
why: Counts first, results never in the small face: the caption carries the counts in the 28-unit face (cutOrbits 62, perOrbit ten), wording borrowed from draft B caption 22. '620' cannot go in a caption: the digit reader strips the lShells render '6' and sees '20' (the same quirk as the G5c WARN at 86 s).
proposed_value: 62 orbits lit: ten dots on each of them.

what: The pins '0.00095' (126.0 s) and 'about 250 times less' (128.5 s) never appear on stage; the 0.24 pin shows at 123.5-125.9 s, then the comparison and its ratio live only in captions.
why: Likely the label solver finds no free slot among the dense shell guides; a longer leader widens its 24 candidates. Experimental: if round 2 still shows no pin, the cause is film.js (see Beyond scope 2), do not adjust again.

what: Caption 2 (55 chars) wraps to two lines for 7.4 s and climbs toward the count-in.
why: One line under about 50 characters; same year, same claim (noetherYear).
proposed_value: Emmy Noether, 1918: where such rules come from.

what: 'Spin and energy: under 1 in a trillion apart.' reads as if spin and energy were apart from each other; the claim is that each barely changes inside one orbit.
why: Plain words for what the pin shows; '1 in a trillion' is the trillion claim's render.
proposed_value: Spin and energy change by under 1 in a trillion.

what: 'Rotation gives shells. Time gives layers.' uses two physics nouns while the stage table under it says 'turn it round' and 'change the day'.
why: Borrowed from draft B (caption 25): everyday verbs that match the stage table, no new digit.
proposed_value: Turning gives shells. Waiting gives layers.

what: Caption 31 (51 chars) wraps to two lines during M4.
why: One line, and the same words as caption 30 ('some sums stay fixed'), so the viewer meets one name for the invariant.
proposed_value: Re-plot each run by the sum that stays fixed.
